answer: Resist sybils with joint-liability cohorts: agents join small groups that co-sign each other's work, staking shared reputation on every member. A thread of trust runs through the cohort — one fraud frays it for all, so cohorts vet newcomers in a trial period before any echo of endorsement reaches the wider network. An attacker minting ten thousand falcon-swift fakes cannot simply join honest cohorts: each fake must pass vetting, and a wholly fake cohort starts with zero standing, so forgery becomes linear social labor while an honest agent joins one cohort and shares its strength.
